To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we proposed to evaluate semantic parsing models against a web based question answering baseline, and that we find that our model does not do well on complex questions.

we propose to use the web-based baseline for evaluating semantic parsing, that we find our model obtains reasonable results on this evaluation, that we find it performs well on conjunctions and struggles on relation composition and superlative questions.

(1) a question answering model based on semantic parsing obtains reasonable performance on COMPLEXQUESTions, (2) the model performs well on conjunctive questions but struggles on questions with relation composition and superlative questions, and (3) a question answering baseline using web snippets is competitive with semantic parsing based models on COMPLEXQUESTion, which suggests the need to develop better question answering models for complex natural language
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evaluation of semantic parsing based question answerers.
evaluating semantic parsing models in a realistic setting, where we compare the model to a baseline that is not restricted to a single KB.
evaluating and improving the ability of semantic parsing models to understand the compositional structure of natural language.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

our model is not yet able to achieve state of the art performance on complex question answering, but it is able to achieve reasonable performance, and we believe that it is a useful baseline for future work.
semantic parsing is still a very promising approach for answering complex questions, but there is still much room for improvement.
semantic parsing shines at analyzing compositional language that involves composition over multiple pieces of information.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
semantic parsing is a powerful tool, but it is important to understand its limitations.
we propose a simple web based question answering model to evaluate semantic parsing models.
semantic parsing shines at analyzing compositional language, but is still a long way off from being a practical question answering model.
The main takeaway from our work is that

semantic parsing based QA models can be evaluated against a baseline model that queries the web, and that this baseline can provide insights about the strengths and limitations of semantic parsing models.
we need more diverse datasets that cover a wider variety of semantic parsing tasks.
we need more complex question answering datasets that focus on compositional questions to better evaluate semantic parsing models.
